solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Type docked round area by island lake?

definitions.text: Type docked round area by island lake?

indicators.note: the shortened word goes round the other letters, enclosing them
a docked tail is cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a type of person is a sort
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone whose ship has tied up near an island by a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a seafaring type docked by an island. 'docked' trims SORT to SOR, which goes 'round' A, I and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaman is exactly the type of person whose vessel gets docked at an island.

clue.text: Most frightening actress I upset

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actress admits she has been unsettled by something terrifying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges ACTRESS and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A superlative synonym: what frightens most is the most alarming of all.

clue.text: Slormgorm is rambling about pressure going up?

indicators.note: the setter's words and the rambling word together go about, enclosing, the pressure letter

parts.note: the setter speaking of themself says I'm, written IM
rambling is wandering about, roving
P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: The setter admits to wandering off the point about pressure rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts P inside IMROVING, after the M. The question mark flags that 'going up' is a loose, figurative sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Something getting better is figuratively on the rise, heading upward in quality.

clue.text: Free love exercises emancipation ultimately

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O
PE is physical education, school exercises

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end, so the final letter of emancipation is taken

explanation.surface: Free love as a practice that ends in liberation.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrestricted or unlocked: something free is not closed off to anyone.

clue.text: Ignoring Duke, empty sink and part of shower

indicators.note: ignoring a letter means leaving it out of the word

parts.note: to empty a vessel is to drain it
to sink is to drop

explanation.surface: Someone skips a nobleman's chores, drains the basin and takes a shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ignoring Duke' removes D from DRAIN, giving RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A single falling bead of water is one small piece of a shower of rain.

clue.text: Splinter groups shunning summit engagements

indicators.note: in a down clue the summit is the top letter, which is avoided here

parts.note: breakaway groups within a party are factions

explanation.surface: Breakaway political groups refuse to attend a summit and its meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shunning summit' drops the top letter F of FACTIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Military engagements are battles, also called actions in army language.

clue.text: A line snorted by one out of habit in Darwin?

indicators.note: something snorted is taken in by the nose, so these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: a nudist is out of any habit, any clothing: a naturist

explanation.surface: A monk out of his habit snorts a line of a drug in Darwin, Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snorted by' puts A and L inside NATURIST. 'Darwin?' is a definition by example, the question mark flagging it.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Darwin is the most famous example of a scientist who studied living things in the wild.

clue.text: Rule for a king German put in check

indicators.note: the German letter is placed inside the word for check

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain

explanation.surface: A German monarch is put in check, as in chess.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's rule is the period of their sovereignty on the throne.

clue.text: Drug dealer one might give the elbow

definitions.meaning: slang for someone who sells illegal narcotics
someone shoving through a crowd, giving people a nudge with the elbow

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the verb to shove: one shoves drugs, the other shoves people aside.

clue.text: Maybe one nibbling your ear in the sack?

definitions.text: Maybe one nibbling your ear in the sack?

parts.words: Maybe one nibbling your ear in the sack?
parts.note: reads like a lover nibbling an ear in bed (the sack), but it is a biting insect that lives in mattresses

explanation.surface: A flirtatious partner nibbling an ear in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the sack' is slang for in bed; the romantic nibbler is really a blood-sucking pest.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect lives in mattresses and bites sleepers, ears included, at night.

clue.text: Time to open a gift? Right now!

definitions.meaning: read literally, the phrase is when you are at a gift, unwrapping it

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means currently, and read literally it places you at a gift, ready to unwrap it.

clue.text: Those who secretly follow stories on radio

indicators.note: something on the radio is heard rather than seen, so the word's sound counts

parts.note: stories are tales

explanation.surface: Detectives who shadow suspects feature in radio dramas.
explanation.definitionFit: To tail someone is to shadow them, so these are people doing covert surveillance.

clue.text: Gun club

definitions.meaning: slang for a pistol or firearm
a golf club with a metal head

explanation.definitionFit: The metal names both a slang pistol and a metal-headed golf club.

clue.text: Can hero be wrong to stifle Republican hatred

indicators.note: the rearranged letters smother the Republican letter, holding it inside
something gone wrong is out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Could a hero wrongly suppress a Republican out of loathing?
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges CAN HERO BE, and 'to stifle' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathing and detestation are close synonyms of this word for intense dislike.

clue.text: Perhaps briefs consider it criminal

indicators.note: criminal acts are crooked, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A lawyer's briefs consider whether the act was criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges CONSIDER IT. 'Perhaps' signals briefs are one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief is a set of instructions, so briefs are an example of guidance on what to do.

clue.text: What one likes doing with son in a bad way

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
someone in a bad way is unwell, ailing

explanation.surface: A parent's favourite pastime spoiled by a son who is unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers to the answer to 1 across: what that seafarer enjoys doing.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a boat out on the water is what a seafarer, the 1 across answer, enjoys.

clue.text: Pale-looking having left first wife, gulp!

indicators.note: the first wife has left, so the earlier of the two wife letters departs from the word

parts.note: to gulp is to swallow

explanation.surface: Someone looks pale after their first wife walked out: gulp!
explanation.walkthrough: 'having left' removes the first of the two Ws in SWALLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A sickly yellowish complexion is described with this word for pallid and wan.

clue.text: Breaking the law is disgusting

explanation.definitionFit: The verb to offend gives both senses: to commit a crime and to cause disgust.

clue.text: Don't start a casual affair or marriage

indicators.note: the word is not allowed to begin, so its first letter goes

parts.note: a dalliance is a casual romantic affair

explanation.surface: Advice against a fling, or against a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't start' removes the D of DALLIANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Marriage is a union, and a union of two parties or families is a formal pact.

clue.text: Say clothing needs bow removed for going out

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated eg

indicators.note: a ship's bow is its front, so the front letter is taken off

parts.note: a dress is an item of clothing

explanation.surface: A dress needs its decorative bow taken off before a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bow removed' drops the front letter D of DRESS, leaving RESS. 'bow' looks like a ribbon but means the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit is a way out, and the word also means the act of leaving.

clue.text: Dexterity? It sounds unimportant!

indicators.note: the clue says the word sounds like the next word, pointing to pronunciation

parts.note: something unimportant is slight

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a skill as a trivial thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight of hand is manual nimbleness, so the word means skill or deftness.

clue.text: Calm displayed by Bucharest fullbacks

indicators.note: the letters are on show within the two words

explanation.surface: The Romanian football team's defenders show composure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed by' finds the letters across BuchaREST FULlbacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Peaceful and soothing are synonyms of this word for tranquil.

clue.text: A fan of metal chair with curved supports

definitions.meaning: a fan of heavy metal or rock music
a chair on curved runners that tilts back and forth

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a hard-rock music devotee and a chair that sways on curved runners.

clue.text: Irate daughter touring Rhode Island city

indicators.note: touring around something goes round it, enclosing it

parts.note: irate means mad, angry
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
RI is the US postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: An angry daughter on a tour of an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' puts MADD round RI, between its two Ds.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Spain's capital, a European metropolis.

clue.text: He attracts flies continuously

indicators.note: something that flies scatters in all directions, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man draws in insects, the way a fly-paper strip does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flies' is the signal, not the insects: it rearranges HE ATTRACTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Without a break or pause, as in working for hours without stopping.

clue.text: Make sense of a theologian in court

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree
up means appearing before a court, as in up before the judge

explanation.surface: Trying to understand a theologian on trial.
explanation.definitionFit: When facts are consistent and logical, they are said to tally or be coherent.

clue.text: One against soprano leaving wine around knight

indicators.note: the shortened wine goes around the knight letter
the soprano leaving means her letter is taken out

parts.note: Asti is an Italian sparkling wine
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A singer who disapproves walks out on the wine served to a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes S from ASTI, giving ATI, which goes 'around' N.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone opposed to an idea is called this, a word for an opponent.

clue.text: Large American sat on yours truly? Painful!

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first letters sit on top of the next

parts.note: L is the clothing abbreviation for large
yours truly is the speaker, me

explanation.surface: A big American sat on the speaker, which hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for feeble or embarrassingly bad, painful to witness, as in a weak excuse.

clue.text: Equine event staff expect order primarily

parts.note: a staff is a rod or stick

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so the opening letters of the next two words are used

explanation.surface: Staff at a horse show expect things to be orderly.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy contest of bronco riding is a show built around horses.

clue.text: Islander reading a novel about Nazi leader

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, around, the chosen letter
novel means new, so these letters are given a new arrangement
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone from an island is reading a book about Hitler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges READING A, and 'about' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Grenada, the Caribbean island nation, is a resident of an island.

clue.text: Warehouses will store silicon for plants

indicators.note: the warehouses hold the other letters inside them

parts.note: depots are storage warehouses
Si is the chemical symbol for silicon

explanation.surface: Storage buildings keep silicon chips for factories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plants' is a verb, not factories or flowers: it means places or puts down.
explanation.definitionFit: To plant something is to set it down, as in placing an item somewhere.

clue.text: Hound bald-headed type after bit of banter

indicators.note: the bird comes after the single letter in the answer
a bit of the word is its first letter

parts.note: the bald eagle, the white-headed American bird

explanation.surface: A dog follows some teasing about a bald man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bald-headed type' suggests a balding man but is the bald eagle.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small breed of hunting dog, a type of hound.
